changeSummary: Corrective rework of CHG-0001 after security-auditor rated the guard CRITICAL-bypassable. Replaced the two raw-text patterns (git stash excluding list/show, git worktree add under .claude/) with argument-level inspection in .claude/hooks/block-dangerous-command.mjs: the command is tokenised the way a shell would tokenise it (quote-aware, operator/command-substitution segments, backslash kept literal for Windows paths), leading environment assignments and transparent wrappers are stripped, nested shell interpreters are recursed into up to depth 3, git global options are resolved (-C, -c, --git-dir, --work-tree, --namespace, --exec-path, --config-env, --super-prefix, in both attached and separated form, plus boolean globals), and the decision is made on the parsed subcommand. The other 15 raw-text patterns are unchanged. The self-test hook assertions were replaced by a 37-case table-driven matrix. This event also discloses the .gitignore change that CHG-0001 omitted from filesChanged.
fileChangeJustification: .claude/hooks/block-dangerous-command.mjs :: replaced the two raw-text patterns with argv-based inspection; also rewritten with LF endings to match the .gitattributes policy after the working copy had drifted to CRLF.

scripts/test-claude-system.mjs :: replaced the 7 ad-hoc hook assertions with a 37-case matrix covering every reported bypass string, the previously correct blocked cases, the allowed read-only cases, and three false-positive cases.

.gitignore :: CHG-0001 modified this file but omitted it from filesChanged, which is the ledger inconsistency the reviewer flagged. Resolution: keep only the .claude/tmp/ rule (one-off JSON payloads handed to the record commands and a backup patch; the durable record is already in the .claude/**/*.jsonl registries) and drop the .claude/worktrees/ rule, accepting the reviewer's objection that ignoring it removes the git status ?? signal that is how a leftover worktree gets noticed.
evidence: BEFORE: the 37-case matrix now committed in scripts/test-claude-system.mjs was executed against the exact pre-change hook (HEAD version plus the two CHG-0001 raw-text patterns) and produced 18/37 pass, 19 fail. All 16 reported bypass strings exited 0 (PASSES), proving the CRITICAL defect was real and that the new cases can fail.
AFTER: the same 37 cases against the argv-based hook produce 37/37 pass, 0 fail. Every bypass string now exits 2.

Bypasses closed (exit 0 -> exit 2): git -C /tmp <sub>; git -c core.x=1 <sub>; git --git-dir=<path> <sub>; git --git-dir <path> <sub>; git --work-tree=<path> <sub>; git --work-tree <path> <sub>; git --namespace=x <sub>; git --exec-path=<path> <sub>; git --no-pager <sub>; git -C /tmp -c core.x=1 --git-dir=/a <sub> push -u; double-quoted subcommand; single-quoted subcommand; global option plus quoted subcommand; and the same -C / -c / --git-dir class against worktree add targeting .claude/.

No over-blocking: git <sub> list, git <sub> show -p <ref>, git -C /tmp <sub> list, git worktree add ../qarga-review-s03 main, git worktree add ../scratch-claude-notes main, and git worktree list all still exit 0.

False positives removed: git commit -m with a message mentioning the phrase, git log --grep for the phrase, and echo of the phrase all exited 2 before and exit 0 after, because a string literal is now an argument of another subcommand rather than raw matched text.
No regression in the untouched patterns: git reset --hard HEAD~1 and git push origin main still exit 2.

knownLimitations: Scope: only the two PROP-0001 destructive-workflow rules use argument-level inspection. The other 15 entries remain raw-text regexes and retain the same bypass class (for example git -C /tmp reset --hard is not blocked, and git commit -m with a message containing the words git restore is still a false positive). This is pre-existing behaviour, was not in the approved scope, and is reported for a separate proposal rather than silently widened.

Base64 or otherwise encoded interpreter payloads (for example pwsh -EncodedCommand) are not decoded, so a deliberately obfuscated invocation is not detected. The hook is a guardrail against ordinary and accidental invocation, not a sandbox against an adversary who controls the command string.

The index must be reconciled by whoever holds git-mutation authority before this is committed.
